title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with a synthetic likeness. Someone on a WhatsApp video call presented himself as a sitting chief minister and used a deepfake to hold that claim up. The failure sits at the point of first contact between a citizen and a person claiming to represent the state, where nothing in the channel establishes who is on the other end.

The scheme escalated in stages, a supposed manager and then a supposed CBI officer, each attaching a new payment to a benefit already promised. The victim paid again to protect money he had already sent, which is the mechanic the fraud depended on. Catching it would have taken an independent check of the caller's identity through an official channel, or a platform-level signal that the face on the call was not a real person, and the reporting does not describe either being available to him.

What is not established is who placed the call, who produced the deepfake, or whether anyone will be charged. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act, which is a registration and not a finding, and the account rests on a single outlet.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29 year old Bengaluru security guard, Ratikanta Giri, lost more than Rs 1 lakh after a WhatsApp video call used a deepfake of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. On Sept 9, the caller introduced himself as Vijay and offered Rs 11 lakh in financial aid. A supposed manager said Rs 5 lakh was allotted and asked Giri to pay fees. Giri first paid Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

Later, someone claiming to be CBI officer Thakur demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Fearing loss of earlier payments, Giri sent more money, with total losses over Rs 1.04 lakh. When the fraudsters asked for another Rs 50,000, he refused and realized he had been duped. He contacted cybercrime helpline 1930 and then Byappanahalli police. A case was registered under the Information Technology Act. This was the first such case reported in the city. Police urged people not to trust such calls or make payments based on them.
